sentences.text: [solemn] A ship once rained gold bars on Bombay, and India's firefighters still remember it every April fourteenth.
It was nineteen forty-four, and the Fort Stikine sat in the docks with fourteen hundred tons of explosives and crates of gold for the bank.
Then cotton in the hold caught fire, and firemen pumped in so much water it started to boil.
So why didn't anyone get the explosives off?
The orders to unload came too late, and that afternoon the ship blew up.
[lowering their voice] More than eight hundred people died, sixty-six of them firemen, and the blast threw gold bars across the city.
Workers were still pulling those bars out of the harbour mud in two thousand eleven, and they had to hand every one to the government.
[matter-of-fact] I think whoever found one should have been allowed to keep it.
